content_md: in his [book on class in America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Class:_A_Guide_Through_the_American_Status_System), Paul Fussell notes that the top and bottom of his 9 class hierarchy are invisible. The top by choice and the bottom out of wretchedness. But it’s interesting that classes 2-8 for the most part _want_ to be seen in the most public sense possible. Being on TV was for long the real American dream. I’m not in class 1 or 9, but I share class 9’s desire to be invisible, at least on larger scales, above subcultural. But power in America (though not wealth) correlates sharply with public visibility above subculture scale, except for the very top. That makes even presidents and showy billionaires class 8. If you’re say class 4-5 or something, you can’t have real power without accepting much more public visibility than you might like.
